item.title: Cyprus lending outpaces GDP expansion as credit growth accelerates
item.description: Cyprus banks pushed credit expansion to 10.5% in November, a reversal from the 0.2% contraction recorded two years earlier, as European Central Bank rate cuts unleashed pent-up lending demand. The surge means lending now outpaces economic growth—credit hit 7.43% in the third quarter whilst the economy expanded 3.6%, Central Bank of Cyprus data shows. The […]

item.title: MEP Fidias Panayiotou apologises for slur against Paralympic athletes
item.description: MEP Fidias Panayiotou issued a public apology on Tuesday after using a derogatory term to describe Paralympic athletes with intellectual disabilities, a move that prompted widespread condemnation. The controversy follows a podcast recorded on 29 November with para-athlete Loizos Chrysanthou. During the interview, Panayiotou referred to athletes in the S14 category as “pellous” (fools/madmen). item.description: The first major Sahara dust episode of 2026 has begun to cover Cyprus, with atmospheric sensors recording record-breaking concentrations that have severely impacted air quality and visibility across the island. item.title: 30-year-old freed by firefighters after motorway crash near Erimi
item.description: A 30-year-old driver was trapped in his vehicle after losing control on the Paphos-Limassol motorway shortly after midnight on Tuesday. The crash happened on the Limassol-bound carriageway after the Erimi exit, police said. Firefighters freed the driver from the wreckage.
